texts.preamble: Kamal Das vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 January, 2020 Author: Sunil Kumar Awasthi Bench: Sunil Kumar Awasthi 1
texts.facts: She has taken the samples of the ice candy and one of the sample was forwarded to State Food Laboratory, Bhopal for examination. The Public Analyst, vide report dated 21/10/2009 found that the said ice candy was adulterated. On the receipt of the said report, Food Inspector- Sushma Pathrod, Dewas has made a request to the competent authority/CMO, Dewas for written consent for launching the prosecution against the applicant and the said permission was granted to the Food Inspector by the CMO, Dewas on 24/10/2009. Thereafter, Food Inspector sent a notice to the applicant under Section 13(2) of the PFA Act and then, she filed the complaint against the applicant for commission of offence punishable under Sections Sections 7(I) and 7(II) read with Section 16(1)(A)(I) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act. 3. The trial court by adopting the summons procedure, read over the particular of offence to the applicant for commission of offence punishable under Sections 7(I) and 7(II) read with Section 16(1)(A)(I) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act. The applicant abjured his guilt and pleaded innocence, however, he has not examined any witness in his defence.
texts.arguments: 5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the independent witnesses of the case did not support the prosecution story and turned hostile. As per the statement of Sushma Patharol (PW 1), she never gives any notice under Sction 13(2) of the PFA Act to the applicant and no dispatch of the said notice has been filed, therefore, the applicant is deprived from his valuable right, which has been conferred upon him for sending the second sample of the said food article to Central Food Laboraty for chemical analysis. Hence, the trial court as well as appellate Court have committed error in convicting the applicant for the aforesaid offence. Under these circumstances, learned counsel for the applicant prays for setting aside of the impugned judgments and acquittal of the applicant. 6. On the other hand, learned Public Prosecutor supported the impugned judgments by contending that all the necessary compliance has been made before launcing the prosecution against the applicant and there is no ground available on record to interfere the concurrents findings recorded by the courts' below. Though, Madhubala (PW 2) did not support the prosecution story and turned hostile, however, from the minute scrutiny of evidence of Sushma Patharol (PW 1), this Court is of the considered view that the courts' below have not committed any error in convicting the applicant for commission of offence punishable under Kamal Das vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145783204/ 2 Sections 7(I) and 7(II) read with Section 16(1)(A)(I) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act. 9.
